text:
Maya: Heads-up — scheduling a planned maintenance for eu-west1 control plane and serving pool on Tue Mar 31 02:00-03:00 UTC. This is a short rolling config push + node rotation. Expected customer-visible risk: small percentage of requests may see 1–3s latency spikes or rare 502s during individual node handoffs. Will run prefix/KV cache warmups afterwards.

Sam: Copy. Are we publishing on the status page and sending a customer advisory? Also need the oncall rotation for the window.

Maya: Yes — draft status page + customer template below. Ops runbook attached inline. Oncall: Sam will be the primary pager 02:00-04:00 UTC, Diego is backup. Jordan, can you sign off on the customer copy? Lee please queue for CS distribution list after I finish.

Jordan: Quick skim — looks good. Suggest we soften "may see 502s" to "brief request failures possible". Also include a link to how to opt for Dedicated if customers ask.

Lee: I can pull the customers with traffic routed through eu-west1 and pre-fill the message. Please flag any enterprise accounts needing account team review.

Diego: ETA on runbook? I want to validate drain steps vs. serving runtime behavior (we have KV cache rebuild window).

Maya: Runbook (short):
1) Preflight (30m prior): healthcheck topology, confirm spare capacity >= 25%, snapshot config, notify status page draft.
2) Drain loop (rolling by AZ): `rctl drain --pool serving-euw1 --grace 120 --parallel 2`
3) Rotate control-plane instances: `gcloud compute instances recreate cp-euw-* --zone=europe-west1-*` (internal deploy)
4) Verify metrics (p50/p95/p99 tokens, 4xx/5xx rates) and prefills. If errors spike >3x baseline for >5m, abort and rollback: `rctl rollback-config --to snap://pre-maint-2151234567`
5) Post-check: run KV warmup: `warmup-kv --pool serving-euw1 --threads 8` and validate tail-latency under 500ms.

Sam: Thanks. Add a step to toggle routing fallback if we exceed error threshold: set routing policy to route 20% of traffic to eu-central1: `routingctl set-fallback --from eu-west1 --to eu-central1 --pct 20`. Also confirm SLO escalation: page oncall-sre if error rate > 5% sustained for 10m.

Maya: Added. Customer-facing status page draft: 
- Status: Maintenance in progress
- Component: Hosted API (eu-west1)
- Impact: Short intermittent latency increases and very rare request failures for customers routed to eu-west1. We expect recovery within the maintenance window.
- Updates: Will post progress at start, midpoint, and completion.

Customer email template (short):
"Hello — We will perform a brief scheduled maintenance in eu-west1 on Tue Mar 31 02:00-03:00 UTC. During the window some requests routed to eu-west1 may see brief latency spikes or rare failures. We do not expect data loss. If you rely on eu-west1 only for low-latency traffic, consider routing resilience options; reach out if you want us to help.

Planned actions: rotating control plane + serving node drain; primary contact: Maya (ops)."

Jordan: Fine to publish as-is with the softened phrasing.

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance ticket created: MAINT-2151234567 (eu-west1 control-plane + serving rotation). /cc @oncall-sre

incident-bot: Paging policy attached: oncall-sre -> Sam (primary), Diego (secondary). Automatic fallback route configured.

Lee: I pushed the customer list. Two enterprise accounts flagged (ACME, Nimbus) — Jordan, can you review messages for those?

Jordan: I'll loop in account reps and add a short line offering a 1:1 technical sync if they want.

Diego: I validated drain command on staging; KV warmup takes ~90s per shard with 8 threads. Will stand by to monitor real run.

Maya: Preflight checklist complete at 01:30 UTC. Spare capacity 32%. Starting maintenance window at 02:00 UTC.

Maya: 02:03 UTC — started draining first AZ. Initial small spike in p99 tokens (from 420ms to 730ms) for ~45s while caches re-warmed. No sustained error increase.

Sam: Watching metrics. Setting routing fallback to 10% as precaution: `routingctl set-fallback --from eu-west1 --to eu-central1 --pct 10`

Maya: 02:20 UTC — rotated cp-euw-1 and cp-euw-2, no customer reports. Continuing roll.

Diego: Observed one short 502 spike at 02:27 UTC for ~30s affecting <0.02% of requests. Logs show transient gRPC timeout during drain. Noted in incident log.

Maya: 02:40 UTC — final AZ done, warming complete. Running post-checks.

Sam: Performing sanity checks against SLOs. p99 back to ~420ms, 5xx rate baseline. No pages triggered.

Maya: 02:45 UTC — maintenance complete. Final note for status page: Completed at 02:45 UTC. Observed a brief, isolated 502 spike affecting a very small percent of requests. No customer-impacting data loss.

Lee: I'll send the post-maint customer email and update the enterprise reps. Draft: "Maintenance completed at 02:45 UTC. We observed a brief transient error spike; if you saw any issues please reply and we'll investigate."

Jordan: LGTM. Add a short postmortem note to ops docs about adjusting drain grace to 180s for future to reduce 502s.

Maya: Filed follow-up ticket: OPS-215123557 (adjust drain grace and monitoring thresholds). Closing maintenance thread and updating status page now. :white_check_mark:

Sam: Thanks everyone. Good run.

Diego: Thumbs up.

deploy-bot: Maintenance MAINT-2151234567 marked complete by Maya at 02:45 UTC.
